hook_text: Why dividing by 0,5 doubles your number
clip_script:
Here is the thing about dividing by a decimal that surprises everyone: the answer gets bigger. Seven comma three five divided by zero comma five. Instead of reaching for a method, ask what the division means: how many halves are there in seven comma three five? Every whole number has two halves in it, so seven has fourteen, and the extra zero comma three five is a bit more than half of a half — about zero comma seven of a half. Fourteen comma seven. Dividing by a half doubled the number, because halves are small and lots of them fit.

That is the picture for every division by a decimal under one. Four comma eight divided by zero comma six: how many six-tenths in four comma eight? Think in tenths: forty-eight tenths, in groups of six tenths — eight groups. And look at what you did: you turned both numbers into tenths.
